Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the MediCore Health Systems Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. As a reminder, please do not place your line on hold as background noise may be transmitted. Today's conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss MediCore Health Systems's financial results for the third quarter. Joining me on the call are Dr. Elena Vasquez, Chief Executive Officer; Mark Thompson, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Lisa Chen, Chief Medical Officer; Raj Patel, Chief Operating Officer; and Dr. Nina Patel, Chief Innovation Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Vasquez.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the third quarter. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on six key aspects: impact of acuity mix changes on revenue, trends in payer mix shifts and their impact on revenue, factors affecting operating margin including revenue growth and cost control, trends in inpatient versus outpatient volumes, supply costs and other operating expenses, and operating margin year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter.

Starting with the impact of acuity mix changes on our revenue, this has been a pivotal factor in our top-line performance, contributing significantly to our 8.2% year-over-year revenue growth to $2.4 billion across our 45-hospital footprint. Acuity mix refers to the blend of patient severity levels, measured by our system-wide Case Mix Index, or CMI. Higher acuity patients, such as those with complex cardiac cases, neuro surgeries, or sepsis admissions, carry heavier DRG weights and higher reimbursements from payers like Medicare, Medicaid, and commercial insurers. In the third quarter, we experienced a favorable shift that added about 150 basis points to our consolidated revenue growth, net of volume. Our adjusted CMI rose 3.8% year-over-year to 1.72, up from 1.66, and this marks the third straight quarter of sequential gains. This came from a 12% increase in high-acuity inpatient volumes, especially in top MS-DRGs like 291 for heart failure with MCC, 470 for major joint replacement without MCC, and 871 for septicemia with RV failure. These made up 22% of our inpatient revenue mix, up from 18% last year, lifting average revenue per admission by 6.1% to $14,200.

Quantifying it, in our inpatient segment—which is 62% of total revenues—this acuity uptick generated an extra $185 million, or 7.7% of segment growth. Including outpatient trends, like more Level 3-5 ED visits turning into higher-reimbursed procedures, we saw a 4.2% lift in net patient revenue per case company-wide. Pro forma, excluding our Q1 divestiture of three low-acuity rural facilities, it would have been 175 basis points stronger.

Post-COVID pent-up demand is still unfolding, with patients presenting later and sicker, raising our average SOI/ROMI scores by 5.2% for Medicare patients due to deferred care from 2020-2022. Aging demographics helped too, with Medicare at 52% of payer mix showing 15% higher acuity, matching CMS national trends up 2.9%. Commercial payers at 28% reimbursed high-acuity DRGs at 142% of Medicare rates versus 120% for low-acuity, a 20% spread, though Medicaid was flat in rural areas.

Regionally, the Northeast with 25% of beds saw CMI up 5.1% from seasonal respiratory cases like pneumonia needing ventilators, adding $45 million and outperforming peers like Universal Health Services by 200 basis points. Southeast at 35% of beds had a 2.9% lift from ortho and vascular lines, boosted by transplants in Atlanta rivaling HCA. Midwest at 20% was at +1.7% due to workforce issues on OBS-to-IP conversions, addressed by tele-ICU. West Coast at 20% gained 4.5% in neuro-oncology, offset somewhat by California Medi-Cal cuts.

We've invested $150 million in clinical documentation improvement using 3M 360 Encompass and Nuance AI, improving query rates 28% and DRG accuracy to 96%, lifting CMI 120 basis points. Epic's acuity forecasting across 80% of facilities predicts admissions 48 hours ahead, cutting LOS 0.4 days on complex cases. Viz.ai partnership for stroke triage reduced door-to-needle by 22%, shifting 15% more to higher DRGs. This outpaced Tenet at 2.1% and Community Health Systems' flat CMI, despite CMS FY24 IPPS boosting high-acuity weights 3.2% but squeezing observations.

Forward, we see acuity mix as a tailwind adding 100-125 basis points to FY24 growth, with 2-3% CMI expansion as demand normalizes. Risks like payer audits are stress-tested, and we're expanding TAVR and CAR-T via JVs with Medtronic and Gilead for 5% CMI lift, plus acuity-based pricing pilots with Blue Cross.

Next, trends in payer mix shifts have shaped our results significantly. Our consolidated payer mix in Q3 was Medicare at 48.2% of net patient revenue, up 210 basis points year-over-year from 46.1%; commercial at 35.4%, down 180 basis points from 37.2%; Medicaid at 11.5%, up 90 basis points; and self-pay/other at 4.9%, flat. This 300 basis point shift toward government payers aligns with peers like HCA and Community Health Systems, and CMS data showing 2-4% migration. Trailing 12-month Medicare is 47.5%, from Baby Boomers at over 25% of admissions.

Acceleration in H2 came from Medicare Advantage enrollment spikes, with MA at 32% of Medicare revenue, up from 28%. Commercial erosion from narrow networks by UnitedHealthcare and Elevance Health.

Net revenue per adjusted patient day, at CMI 1.72, fell 1.8% to $2,145. Medicare at $1,890 down 0.5% from flat IPPS and 15% MA clawbacks; commercial $2,980 down 3.2% from OON suppression; Medicaid $1,420 up 1.1% from supplements; self-pay $1,650 down 2% from charity care. This shaved $85 million or 2.1% off revenue, offset 60% by 4.2% volume growth and 1.5% DRG boost from SDoH codes. EBITDA margins expanded 150 basis points to 18.4%. Kaufman Hall notes 1-3% headwind industry-wide from MA denials.

Southeast (55% beds, Florida/Georgia): Medicaid up 150 bps to 14.2% from redetermination delays, commercial hit by Florida Blue, revenue per APD flat at $2,180. Midwest (30%, Ohio/Kentucky): Medicare 52%, Kentucky expansion added 2% volume. Texas outposts (15%): low Medicaid 7%, self-pay up from migrants, commercial ASPs down 4.5%.

We're accelerating value-based care with 25% commercial under risk-sharing like ortho bundles with Humana/Cigna, $12 million ACO REACH savings. Revenue cycle with Epic Denial Prevention cut denials to 8.5%, cash to 45 days; 3M AI captured $25 million HCCs. Renegotiated 15 contracts for 2.5% uplifts, targeting 30% MA by 2025. Expanding ASCs to 35 sites with 60% commercial mix, partnerships like Oscar for bundles.

Modeling Medicare to 52% by 2026, focusing on scale via Vizient, labor productivity, SDoH for waivers. ASC pivot like Tenet validates. Payer shifts a $300-400 million challenge, but 65% offset keeps 5-6% FY23 growth.

Turning to factors affecting operating margin, we hit 12.8%, up 160 basis points year-over-year from 11.2%, strongest since pre-pandemic, beating HCA at 12.1% and Tenet at 11.5%. Revenue grew 9.2% to $2.85 billion from 6.1% patient days, 7.2% admissions in cardiology/ortho. CMI to 1.68 from 1.62 via Medtronic robotics cutting LOS 0.4 days.

Commercial at 48% up from 45%, Medicare 4.8% growth navigated 2.7% IPPS cut via 32% MA. Revenue per admission up 2.9% to $14,200 at 95.8% collections. Southeast grew 12%, ASCs $120 million at 25%+ margins. OpEx to 87.2% from 91.4%, 4.2 point leverage.

Labor 44.5% from 47.1%, HPPD to 8.9 from 9.4, CareForward upskilled 2,500 LPNs, Cerner AI cut overtime 18%, contract labor down 35% QoQ to 1.6%. Supplies 19.8% via Vizient 7% savings, biosimilars cut rheum 22%, vendors to 850 saving $28 million. IT $15 million savings, Epic Hyperdrive 75% rollout, cash to 97 days. Telehealth up 45% to 250,000, virtual nursing cut readmits 12%, 28% value-based.

Outlook: 13-14% by year-end, 55% non-acute revenue by 2025. Risks MA cuts, unions, but $200 million buyback.

On trends in inpatient vs. outpatient volumes, inpatient admissions 142,000 down 2.8% YoY, better than HCA's 3.5%, patient days 785,000 down 1.2%, ALOS 5.5 from 5.8, CMI up 1.4% to 1.72, revenue per admission up 4.1% to $14,200. Outpatient 1.8 million encounters up 6.7% YoY, 2.1% QoQ: ASCs 245,000 up 8.2%, observations 98,000 up 12%, ortho 15%, GI 9% with Boston Scientific. Revenue per visit $1,850 up 3.5%.

Sunbelt (Texas/Florida/Arizona): outpatient 9.1%, inpatient flat via ERAS. Northeast/Midwest: inpatient down 4.6% from Medicaid, outpatient 7% via SCA JVs. Post-COVID electives 5-7% below 2019, outpatient up 11%. Nursing at 92% inpatient pushing outpatient.

$450 million in outpatient: 12 ASCs with Stryker Mako, hospital-at-home 15,000 days with Philips, outpatient margin 28% vs. 18%. Humana/Elevance bundles for 20% ortho. Expect inpatient down 1-2%, outpatient 6-8%, $2.5 billion M&A for ASCs.

Regarding supply costs and other operating expenses, total supplies $1.42 billion up 6.2% YoY, 18.4% of revenue vs. 17.6%, sequential from 18.7%. Other op ex $892 million up 4.1%, 11.5% flat. 29.9% total amid 4.8% volumes, 2.1% revenue per case.

Supplies from 3.9% inpatient days to 1.12 million, 4.1% inflation vs. Vizient 3.8%, pharma up 8.5% to $456 million from GLP-1s at 12%, ortho/cardio $312 million up 7.2%. Southeast 19.2% from hurricane logistics, Midwest 17.8%.

Savings $68 million: HealthTrust 92% coverage 2.4% discounts, GHX/Oracle AI cut stockouts 34%/waste 22%, ortho sets to 14, 65% generics/340B. Q4 inflation 3-3.5%. Other op ex: facilities $22 million up 5.8% from gas/HVAC, IT/pro $214 million up 6.3% cyber/EMR, malpractice $12 million up 9%.

Leverage: op ex per admission down 1.2% to $2,910 via Siemens energy 8%, RPA for fees. Outpatient lowers intensity 15-20%. Contributed 60 bps to 12.4% margin, 1-2% quarterly gains.

Finally, operating margin at 14.2%, up 260 bps QoQ from 11.8%, 240 bps YoY from 11.8%, high end vs. Kaufman Hall 10-12%. YoY revenue up 8.7% to $2.45 billion, days 6.2%, CMI 4.5% to 1.98, op income $348 million up 28%.

Supplies up 4.1% below inflation via HealthTrust $45 million, biosimilars 22%. Labor up 7.2% but contract down 15%, upskilling 4,200, PerfectServe to 94% fills. Commercial 58%, MS-DRG 3.8%, $28 million No Surprises. Southeast 17.4% up 16.1% from Medicaid volumes, Midwest 12.8% up 180 bps.

QoQ 260 bps from seasonality, no Q2 cyber $22 million, revenue up 3.4%, admissions 2.1%, observations 12% from 150 urgent cares $180 million. Op ex up 1.2%, Epic RCM denials to 4.2%. Da Vinci in 65 ORs up margins 8%, UnitedHealthcare $15 million savings.

Margin Resilience 2025: ASCs 22% EBITDA to 30%, tele-ICU 70% beds down vents 18%, capitated BCBS Texas. Q4 14.5-15.0%, $50 million gains. Liquidity $1.2 billion.

Now, I’ll turn the call over to Mark to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

Mark Thompson:
Thank you, Dr. Vasquez. Good morning, everyone. As Dr. Vasquez mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Net revenue for the third quarter was $2.4 billion, an increase of 8.2% compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by increased patient volume, favorable payer mix, and the successful implementation of our revenue cycle management initiatives.

Our operating expenses were $2.1 billion, representing 87.5% of net revenue. We are continuing to focus on managing our costs effectively while investing in key growth initiatives, particularly in supply chain optimization.

Net income for the quarter was $250 million, or $1.25 per share. We are pleased with our financial performance and remain confident in our ability to achieve our financial goals for the year.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Chen for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Lisa Chen:
Thank you, Mark. Good morning. We are making significant progress in improving clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction. Our Enhanced Recovery After Surgery program has shown promising results, with a 15% reduction in readmission rates. We are also focused on leveraging technology to enhance the patient experience and improve care coordination, specifically through our telehealth platform.

Following that, Raj will provide an update on operational efficiency.

Raj Patel:
Thank you, Dr. Chen. We are focused on streamlining our operations and improving efficiency across our network. We have implemented several initiatives, including AI-driven scheduling and revenue cycle management streamlining, which have resulted in significant cost savings.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Nina Patel for an overview of our innovation efforts.

Dr. Nina Patel:
Thank you, Raj. We are committed to driving innovation across our organization. We are investing in new technologies and partnerships to improve patient care, enhance efficiency, and create new revenue streams. Our current projects include AI predictive analytics for bed management and telehealth expansion for remote monitoring, which directly address workforce shortages.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to Dr. Vasquez.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Dr. Patel. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you elaborate on the specific cost savings achieved through the implementation of AI-driven scheduling?

Raj Patel:
Good morning, John. Absolutely. Our AI-driven scheduling initiative, powered by Cerner and PerfectServe integrations, has generated approximately $45 million in savings this quarter by optimizing shift fill rates to 94%, reducing overtime by 18%, and cutting contract labor utilization by 35% quarter-over-quarter. This has improved our hours per patient day by 3.2 points system-wide, particularly in high-volume inpatient units, while maintaining care quality standards.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Lee with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Sarah Lee:
What are your expectations for the impact of telehealth on your revenue and patient access?

Dr. Lisa Chen:
Thanks, Sarah. Telehealth is a game-changer for us, with volumes up 45% year-over-year to 250,000 encounters. We expect it to contribute $150-200 million in incremental revenue in FY24, driven by a 20% increase in virtual nursing and hospital-at-home programs that have reduced readmissions by 12%. Patient access has improved dramatically, especially in rural markets, with 48-hour response times and integration into our Epic platform enabling seamless care coordination. Margins here are strong at 25-30%, supporting overall growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Johnson with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson:
Can you provide more details on your plans for investing in new technologies and partnerships?

Dr. Nina Patel:
Hi Mike. We're allocating $450 million over the next 18 months, with key focuses on AI predictive analytics via Nuance and Viz.ai partnerships, which have already lifted CMI by 120 basis points and cut stroke door-to-needle times by 22%. New JVs with Medtronic for TAVR robotics and Gilead for CAR-T aim to expand high-acuity lines, targeting 5% CMI growth. Telehealth expansions with Philips and GHX for supply AI will address shortages, projecting $100 million in efficiency gains and new revenue from value-based bundles.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the MediCore Health Systems Q3 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
